correctness.rationale: For arbitrary finite simple G, invariant barycentric coordinates produce the simplicial orbit complex; lifted copies of every forest component are two trees, linked by selected diagonal edges. More than one such link per component creates a cycle and at most one never does. The same condition exactly characterizes cone forests, proving a natural Aut(G)-equivariant simplicial model. The finite verifier checks 82 graphs and 49,302 orbit subsets, independently corroborating but not replacing the universal proof.

originality.rationale: Novelty comparison is statement-level: published matroid independence shellability and cone homology determine individual homotopy types but not these geometric involution fixed spaces; a complete \(K_{2,n}\) integral homology module concerns a different family and no PL fixed set; a complete prism matching-complex fixed-space theorem uses degree-one constraints instead of forest-cycle constraints. No exact model was found by targeted semantic searches. An unindexed equivalent statement remains a risk, so this is best-knowledge originality, not priority certification.
residual_risks: There may be an equivalent, unindexed statement under voltage graphs, signed-graphic matroids or rooted-forest orbit matroids.
Classical Kook work treats homology of coned graph matroids, though no statement-level implication to the present fixed-space PL model was established from available evidence.
published-finding corpus semantic search and exact source inspection do not prove worldwide publication novelty.

value.rationale: A universal natural and equivariant PL model for geometric fixed spaces of graphical matroid independence complexes, with exact all-graph scope, is a structural fixed-space theorem rather than a routine independent-set restatement. It transfers known matroid topology and natural graph automorphism actions to an infinite family of geometric fixed spaces. Classical wedge ranks are identified as known and are not the novelty claim.
